The '''Brigand''' (Japanese: {{hl|山賊|Sanzoku}} ''Mountainthief'') is a class of [[axe]]-wielding fighters who travel on foot. They first appear in {{FE2}} as an enemy-only class internally using [[sword]]s, as axes do not exist in ''Gaiden''.

The Brigand is traditionally an enemy-only class, with the exceptions being {{FE5}}, in which playable character [[Marty]] is a brigand; {{FE6}}, in which [[Gonzalez]] is a brigand; and {{FE16}}, where the Brigand is a standard promotion option for all playable units. In most games, they can cross mountains.

Brigands generally have low stats in all categories, but above average HP and strength. As enemies, they are not at all difficult to defeat. However, playable brigands often have better stats than those of enemies. Their ability to cross mountains can be useful.

In {{title|Thracia 776}}, brigands can change class to the [[Warrior]] class. In {{title|The Binding Blade}}, brigands become [[Berserker]]s. In the coding for {{title|The Blazing Blade}} and {{title|The Sacred Stones}}, Brigands still promote to Berserker, but this can only be seen via hacking the game.

Similar criminal axe classes are [[Pirate]], [[Bandit]], and [[Barbarian]].

===''Genealogy of the Holy War''===
The class a unit changes into in ''Genealogy of the Holy War'' is determined by the unit and not the class; however, no units change into or out of the Brigand class.
{{Class Change 1
|sprite=[[File:Bs fe04 enemy brigand axe.png]]
|class=Brigand
}}

===''Thracia 776''===
The class a unit changes into in ''Thracia 776'' is determined by the unit and not the class; however, all units in the Brigand class have the following class change option:
{{Class Change 2
|sprite1=[[File:Bs fe05 marty brigand axe.png]]
|basic class=Brigand
|promotion method=Using a {{Item|5|Knight Proof}} at level&nbsp;10 or higher.
|sprite2=[[File:Bs fe05 marty warrior axe.png]]
|promoted class=Warrior
}}

==Trivia==
*In {{title|Gaiden}}, Brigands are internally the same class as [[Villager]]s; whether a unit is a Villager or a Brigand is determined by its affiliation.
* In {{FE3}}, Brigands and Fighters have the same sprites.
* An unused string for the Brigand exists in {{title|New Mystery of the Emblem}}. The string is named <code>MJID_KLEPHT</code>, in reference to the [[wikipedia:klepht|klepht]]s of Ottoman Greece.
